identity.title: Rotating ionized gas ring around the Galactic center IRS13E3
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of Japan

paper_type_evidence.quote: We detected a compact ionized gas associated physically with IRS13E3, an Intermediate Mass Black Hole (IMBH) candidate in the Galactic Center, in the continuum emission at 232 GHz and H30$\alpha$ recombination line using ALMA Cy.5 observation

evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, we adopt 8.0 kpc as the distance to the Galactic center

question.value: Is there a rotating ionized gas ring around IRS13E3 that would give a reliable enclosed mass supporting an intermediate-mass black hole?

evidence.quote: If IRS13E3 is an IMBH, an ionized gas ring would be rotating around it.
We have searched such ionized gas with ALMA in order to prove our hypothesis that IRS13E3 is an IMBH.
using ALMA Cy.5 observation (2017.1.00503.S, P.I. M.Tsuboi)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 4 spectral windows centered at 217.5, 219.5, 234.0, 231.9 GHz; last covers H30alpha; 2.0 GHz coverage, 15.625 MHz resolution (~20 km/s)

evidence.quote: The center frequencies of the spectral windows are $f_c=217.5, 219.5, 234.0,$ and $231.9$ GHz, respectively.
The frequency coverage and frequency resolution are 2.0 GHz and 15.625 MHz, respectively.
The last spectral window covers the H30$\alpha$ recombination line (231.9 GHz).

configurations.value: longest baseline antenna configuration of ALMA

evidence.quote: The observation epochs were in the period of the longest baseline antenna configuration of ALMA.

angular_resolution.value: 0.037" x 0.025", PA=85 deg (continuum, natural weighting); 0.037" x 0.024", PA=87 deg (channel maps)

evidence.quote: The angular resolution using “natural weighting" is $0\ensuremath{''}.037 \times 0\ensuremath{''}.025, PA=85^\circ$

sensitivity.value: channel maps 1 sigma = 90 uJy/beam (2.3 K); continuum 1 sigma = 50 uJy/beam (1.3 K)

evidence.quote: $1\sigma=90~ \mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ or 2.3 K in $T_\mathrm{B}$ in the emission-free areas
The sensitivity is $1\sigma=50~ \mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ or 1.3 K in $T_\mathrm{B}$ in the emission-free areas.
The observations were performed in ten days from 5 Oct. 2017 to 20 Oct. 2017.

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image continuum and H30alpha cube

method.value: uvcontsub on combined data, CASA clean channel maps (20.2 km/s); continuum from line-free data of first seven days with baselines <11 km plus self-calibration

evidence.quote: We used only the data of the first seven days to produce the resultant continuum map here.
`uvcontsub (fitorder=1)`

analysis_steps.goal: Measure size and flux of the oval structure

method.value: two-dimensional Gaussian fit with beam size correction

evidence.quote: by the two-dimensional Gaussian fit including beamsize correction
we adopt 8.0 kpc as the distance to the Galactic center

analysis_steps.goal: Derive enclosed mass from PV diagram

method.value: Rotation velocity from ends of inclined linear feature in PV diagram along major axis, corrected for thermal broadening; inclination from aspect ratio; M = r V_rot^2 / G

evidence.quote: The inclination angle is derived to be $i \sim 50^\circ$ from the aspect ratio of the Gaussian-fit angular size mentioned in Results.
$V_\mathrm{rot}\sim150/\cos{i}$ km/s

assumptions.value: gas on a single circular orbit

evidence.quote: Assuming that the ionized gas obeys a single circular orbit simply

validation.value: Cross-check with free-fall mass of south extended flow, M ~1.0e4/(cos j)^2 Msun, roughly consistent

evidence.quote: This is roughly consistent with the enclosed mass mentioned above.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive electron temperature, density and gas mass

method.value: LTE Te from H30alpha line-to-continuum ratio solved iteratively; ne from brightness temperature (Altenhoff formula); mass from sphere of diameter L

evidence.quote: The LTE electron temperature is obtained by iteratively solving the formula for $T^\ast_{\mathrm e}$.
$\frac{N(\mathrm{He^+})}{N(\mathrm{H^+})}=0.09$

assumptions.value: optically thin line and continuum; spherical geometry with L ~1.14e16 cm

evidence.quote: assuming that the line and continuum emissions are optically thin

used_for.value: data analysis, uvcontsub, clean imaging, self-calibration

evidence.quote: We performed the data analysis by Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA)

results_numeric.quantity: Oval structure angular size (maj x min)

evidence.quote: $0.093\ensuremath{''}\pm0.006\ensuremath{''}\times 0.061\ensuremath{''}\pm0.004\ensuremath{''}$

results_numeric.quantity: Total continuum flux density of oval at 232 GHz

evidence.quote: The total flux density of the oval-like structure is $S_\nu=10.52\pm0.90$ mJy.
Then the rotating velocity is estimated to be $V_\mathrm {rot} \sim 230$ km s$^{-1}$.
the enclosed mass is estimated to be $M\sim2.4\times10^4$ $M_\odot$
$\bar{T}_{\mathrm e}=6800\pm700$ K
The mean electron density is $\bar{n}_{\mathrm e}=6\times10^5$ cm$^{-3}$
$M=\frac{4\pi}{3}\big(\frac{L}{2}\big)^3\bar{n}_{\mathrm e}m_{\mathrm{H}}=4\times10^{-4} M_\odot$
the lower limit of the mass density is estimated to be $\rho \gtrsim8\times10^{11}  M_\odot pc^{-3}$

findings_qualitative.value: IRS13E3 is resolved into an oval structure also seen in H30alpha, with a velocity gradient along its major axis.

evidence.quote: The components positionally shift from northeast to southwest along the major axis of the oval-like structure with increasing velocity.

claims.hypothesis: IRS13E3 hosts a rotating ionized gas ring around a massive object
claims.experiment: 232 GHz continuum and H30alpha imaging with ALMA; PV diagram along major axis
claims.result: Inclined linear PV feature, V_rot ~230 km/s, r ~6e15 cm
claims.finding: Ring rotates around a ~2.4e4 Msun enclosed mass, consistent with an IMBH

evidence.quote: The observed feature may be a part of an ionized gas ring rotating around IRS13E3.

claims.hypothesis: The enclosed mass is compatible with an IMBH rather than a normal cluster
claims.experiment: Density estimate and comparison with X-ray counterpart and astrometric limits
claims.result: rho >~ 8e11 Msun/pc^3; X-ray counterpart within error circle
claims.finding: Supporting evidence for an IMBH; a cluster would collapse within 1e7 yr

evidence.quote: Of course, massive compact objects do not uniquely imply BHs

why_this_method.value: A simple rotating ring gives a more reliable enclosed mass than the complicated Keplerian orbit

evidence.quote: If the rotating ring is discovered, the enclosed mass derived with the simple structure must be reliable.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Compact cluster of stars or remnants as alternative to a black hole

evidence.quote: the alternate may be a compact cluster of star or star remnant and so on

limitations_admitted.value: Sidelobes of Sgr A* worsen sensitivity and remain in the continuum map; variability of Sgr A* limits data use

evidence.quote: Although the sidelobe effects still remain around Sgr A$^\ast$, the dynamic range reaches to $>40000$ in the other areas of the map.

referee_caveats_inferred: Rotation inferred from a single PV diagram with 20 km/s resolution; no kinematic model fit or uncertainty on mass
Inclination from the aspect ratio assumes a circular ring
Gas ring may be non-gravitational flow or part of the larger flow
